title: Llegar a + Infinitive: Reaching a Point

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *llegar a* + infinitive from B2 Unit 25: it says that someone or something gets as far as doing something, often after a long process (*llegó a hablar cuatro idiomas*), and *si llega a* + infinitive means "if it happens to". Both help to tell the story of a grape and of a water supply.

sections.title: Llegar a in Mendoza
rows: El malbec llegó a convertirse en la uva más conocida del país.
Algunas viñas llegan a estar a mucha altura.
an extreme: some vineyards even reach great height
Si llega a faltar nieve, hay menos agua.
*si llega a* + infinitive: if it happens to be missing; the verb after *si* is present
No llegó a ser una región famosa hasta el siglo XX.
with *no*: it did not get as far as becoming famous

items.spanish: Con el tiempo, el malbec llegó a convertirse en la uva más conocida del país.
items.english: In time, Malbec became the best-known grape of the country.

items.spanish: Algunas viñas llegan a estar a mucha altura.
items.english: Some vineyards get to be at a great height.

items.spanish: Si llega a faltar nieve en invierno, hay menos agua en verano.
items.english: If there happens to be little snow in winter, there is less water in summer.

items.spanish: El viaje llegó a ser largo, pero valió la pena.
items.english: The trip ended up being long, but it was worth it.

sections.content: After *llegar a* the verb is an infinitive; after *si llega a* it stays in the present, never the future: *si llega a faltar*, not *si llegará a faltar*. Do not confuse it with *llegar a* + place (*Llegó a Mendoza*), where it simply means "arrived".
